name: Project Charter
one_liner: The what, how and when — the baseline progress is measured against.
purpose: The Project Charter provides the basis for more detailed project planning: it defines the project's objectives in scope, time, cost and quality, its high-level requirements, risks and constraints, and its milestones and deliverables. A vital element of the project approval process, it carries the what, how and when fundamentals of the project and provides a baseline against which progress can be measured. Although the Business Manager may initiate it, completing it and submitting it for approval is ultimately the Project Manager's responsibility.
meta: IT governance artefact — mandatory for projects with an information system (p.25)
The PM² Project Charter itself — there is no separate 'agile charter'
Unchanged PM² template; the agile guide refers you to the PM² Portal and Guide
Project Manager (PM) — Responsible for completing and submitting it
PM² eight-column set (AGB·PSC·PO·BM·UR·SP·PM·PCT), not the agile six
Work Items List — its Features list is the key generator of work items (p.76)

diagram.sec: How the agile layer uses it
items: Features written at high abstraction so every layer understands the scope (p.31)
Features prioritised using business value and size; higher-risk features go first (p.31)
PM is accountable for the WIL staying aligned with charter scope (p.76)
Release Plan and Iteration Goal must trace back to its milestones (pp.77, 79)
Updated versions accompany ad hoc status reporting when scope shifts (p.86)

fields.what: The project's objectives in scope, time, cost and quality — the four dimensions progress is judged on.
fields.pollux: One portal, €4.6 m, 18 months, figures reconciled to the accounts and traceable to source.

fields.what: What is included and what is explicitly excluded, closed by a one- or two-line scope statement.
fields.pollux: IN: exposure reporting portal. OUT: changes to the CASTOR lending platform itself, and payment processing.

fields.what: Stakeholder and user needs, each with an ID, a description and a priority — not yet stories.
fields.pollux: N1 Board one-pager, N2 Risk stress scenarios, N3 Finance reconciliation, N4 national-authority access.

fields.what: A proposed service addressing a business, customer or user need; described with related need and deliverable.
fields.pollux: F1 member-state exposure view, F2 instrument and maturity views, F3 scenario overlay, F4 self-service builder.

fields.what: The Charter's Features list is the key generator of the work items that populate the Work Items List (p.76).
fields.who: PrOw decomposes · PM accountable for alignment
fields.pollux: Curie decomposed F1 into eleven user stories and three enablers before iteration 1.

fields.what: Carried from the Business Case; the measurable statements the project will be judged to have met or missed.
fields.pollux: SC1–SC5 restated verbatim from the Business Case, with baselines and targets unchanged.

fields.what: Named deliverables with descriptions; releases later deliver parts of them incrementally.
fields.pollux: Portal application, reconciled data layer, national-authority access zone, user and operations documentation.

fields.what: What the project cannot change and what it is taking as true; both feed the Release Plan's visible assumptions.
fields.pollux: Constraint: no change to CASTOR schemas. Assumption: two-week iterations with a stable team of eight.

fields.what: High-level risks with likelihood, impact, level, owner and response strategy; refined later in the Risk Log.
fields.pollux: R3: data-engineering knowledge concentrated in one team member (Babbage) — mitigation is pairing.

fields.what: Cost by budget line and year, and milestones with target delivery dates — the baseline for progress.
fields.pollux: €4.6 m; milestones from Charter approval 12 Oct 2028 to administrative closure 20 Mar 2030.

fields.what: The resource requirements the project is approved to consume, including the delivery team's shape.
fields.pollux: In-house team of six plus two seconded members; Eiffel leads the Levallois Systems secondment.

fields.what: Section 5.1 declares the methodology and any deviation from PM² — where 'this project is PM²-Agile' is recorded.
fields.pollux: Declared PM²-Agile: PM² governance and gates kept; Executing run as two-week iterations.

fields.what: Project change, configuration management and organisational change; agile shifts change management towards stakeholder collaboration.
fields.pollux: Changes below one release's scope handled by re-prioritising the WIL; anything moving a gate goes to the PSC.

fields.what: The project organigram and the roles and responsibilities — this is where the A-PCT joins the PM² organisation.
fields.pollux: A-PCT added: Curie (PrOw), Lovelace (TeCo), Einstein (ArOw), Lamarr, Babbage and Eiffel (ATeM).

fields.what: The Charter is the baseline progress is measured against; iteration and release goals must trace back to it.
fields.pollux: Every POLLUX release goal cites the feature and the charter milestone it satisfies.

fields.what: Ad hoc status reporting may carry an updated Charter, showing what evolved since the initial version and why (p.86).
fields.pollux: Charter v1.3 accompanied the Q3 2029 progress report after the scenario overlay moved into Release 3.

fields.what: AGB I · PSC A · PO C · BM S · UR C · SP S · PM R · PCT C. Eight PM² columns, not six.
fields.pollux: The PM completes and submits it; the Steering Committee approves it on 12 Oct 2028.

traps: The PSC is Accountable, not the PO — that was the Business Case.
The BM may initiate the Charter, but the PM completes and submits it.
The Charter holds Features; the Work Items List holds stories — not the same list.
PM²-Agile writes no separate charter; the PM² Project Charter is used unchanged.
Appendix B.2 prints only BM = S and PM = R, with no Accountable.
